title: Voqal Partners Fellowship 2027: Apply for $30,000 to Build Bold Social Justice Ideas
summary: The Voqal Partners Fellowship 2027 is now accepting applications from social justice changemakers in the United States who have bold, early-stage ideas aimed at creating meaningful social change. The six-month fellowship provides selected fellows with a $30,000 award , a $1,000 healthcare stipend , coaching and mentorship, peer support, and fully funded travel to three in-person fellowship convenings. Unlike many traditional funding opportunities, the Voqal Partners Fellowship is specifically designed for people who are still developing an idea. Applicants do not need to have an established organization, completed product, fully developed campaign, or comprehensive business plan. Instead, Voqal Partners is interested in individuals who recognize a systemic problem, have a compelling vision for changing it, and are ready to begin testing, developing, and learning from their idea. Applications for the 2027 cohort close on October 31, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time . Opportunity Overview Opportunity: Voqal Partners Fellowship 2027 Category: Fellowship Fellowship duration: Six months Award: $30,000 Healthcare support: $1,000 healthcare stipend Additional support: Coaching, mentorship, peer learning and community Travel: Fully funded travel to three in-person convenings Childcare support: Available for fellows with dependents under 18 Location requirement: United States Project focus: Social justice and systemic change Application deadline: October 31, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time Fellowship period: April–September 2027 What Is the Voqal Partners Fellowship? The Voqal Partners Fellowship is a six-month program designed to support people who are developing ambitious ideas for social justice and systemic change. The fellowship recognizes that many potentially transformative ideas never receive funding because they are considered too early, too unconventional, or too difficult to fit into traditional philanthropic funding models. Voqal Partners takes a different approach by supporting people at the dream or idea stage and giving them the resources and environment they need to explore what their ideas could become. The program is therefore not necessarily looking for applicants with an established nonprofit organization or an already successful initiative. An applicant may still be determining the best structure for their project, testing assumptions, exploring a new approach, or figuring out how a promising idea could be implemented. The central question is whether the applicant has a strong vision for creating a more equitable future and a realistic starting point for exploring that vision. During the fellowship, selected fellows receive financial support, coaching, mentorship, peer learning opportunities, and access to a community of other changemakers. The program is intended to help fellows move their ideas from an early concept toward real-world experimentation. What Does the $30,000 Fellowship Award Cover? Each selected fellow receives a $30,000 award , generally distributed as a lump sum at the beginning of the fellowship. One of the distinctive features of the Voqal Partners Fellowship is the flexibility attached to the funding. Fellows are not restricted to spending the money only on narrowly defined project expenses. The funding can support expenses such as: Living expenses Equipment Contractors or additional assistance Travel Project implementation Research and experimentation Other costs that help the fellow develop their idea If a particular expense helps the fellow move their idea forward, it is generally considered an appropriate use of the fellowship funding. Voqal Partners can also work with fellows who prefer to receive their funding according to a particular schedule, such as through monthly payments. The organization indicates that the full award can be distributed according to an agreed timeline as long as the entire amount is provided by the end of the fellowship. This flexible funding structure allows fellows to determine what they need most during the six-month period rather than having every expense predetermined by the funder. $1,000 Healthcare Stipend In addition to the $30,000 fellowship award, selected fellows receive a $1,000 healthcare stipend . This additional support recognizes that personal wellbeing and health can affect a person s ability to pursue demanding social justice work. The stipend provides an additional financial resource for fellows during the fellowship period. Fully Funded Travel to Three Fellowship Convenings The fellowship includes three in-person convenings scheduled during the program. These gatherings are an important component of the fellowship because they provide opportunities for fellows to: Meet and learn from other fellows Participate in peer learning Work with coaches and advisors Develop relationships with members of the Voqal community Reflect on their work Collaborate around challenges and opportunities Strengthen their ideas through collective learning Voqal Partners covers the travel costs associated with these gatherings. Fellows with dependents under the age of 18 can also receive childcare support, helping reduce one of the practical barriers that can prevent caregivers from participating fully in professional development and fellowship programs. Coaching, Mentorship and Professional Support Financial support is only one part of the Voqal Partners Fellowship. Selected fellows gain access to coaches, advisors and mentors who can help them think through the challenges involved in turning an early-stage idea into something that can be tested in the real world. This support can include discussions around: Strategy Operations Organizational development Structural challenges Project development Experimentation Leadership Community engagement Future opportunities Because fellows may be working on ideas that challenge existing systems, the coaching component can provide an important opportunity to examine assumptions, identify obstacles and determine practical next steps. A Small Cohort of Social Justice Changemakers Voqal Partners selects only eight fellows each year . The small cohort model allows fellows to develop close relationships with one another and create a community around shared learning. Rather than going through the fellowship experience independently, participants learn alongside other people who are also attempting to develop ambitious ideas for social change. Past fellows remain connected through an active alumni network, creating opportunities for relationships and knowledge-sharing to continue after the formal six-month fellowship ends. Who Is Voqal Partners Looking For? The Voqal Partners Fellowship is aimed at people who are deeply connected to the communities and issues they are working to address. The organization emphasizes that applicants should not simply approach communities from the outside with solutions. Instead, it prioritizes people who are part of the communities they serve and who have a strong understanding of the challenges those communities face. Voqal Partners particularly values: Community leaders Organizers Builders Visionaries People with lived experience People developing unconventional approaches to social justice Individuals working alongside communities affected by systemic problems People seeking to support historically excluded communities The fellowship also encourages applications from individuals and communities that have traditionally had difficulty accessing philanthropic funding. These include, among others: LGBTQIA+ individuals Women Indigenous peoples People of color People with disabilities The emphasis is not simply on demographic identity. Voqal Partners also wants to understand an applicant s relationship with the community, their lived experience, their vision for change, and their ability to contribute meaningfully to the work. What Does Dream-Stage or Idea-Stage Mean? One of the most important aspects of the Voqal Partners Fellowship is its focus on dream-stage and idea-stage projects . This means applicants do not necessarily need to have everything figured out before applying. For example, an applicant might: Have identified a major social problem but still be determining the best solution. Have a new approach they want to test. Be exploring how a community-led initiative could work. Have an early concept for a campaign or project. Have an idea for disrupting an existing system. Be developing a new model for organizing or community participation. Need time and resources to determine whether an unconventional idea can work. The fellowship is designed to provide space for this kind of exploration. Applicants should therefore avoid assuming that their idea is too early simply because they do not yet have a finished organization, product, campaign or business plan. What Types of Projects Does Voqal Partners Support? Voqal Partners seeks ideas that have the potential to challenge or disrupt systems rather than simply making existing systems easier to navigate. The organization is particularly interested in projects with a compelling vision for the future. Projects may be: Hyperlocal Community-based National in scope However, the work must focus on communities in the United States . The scale of the project is therefore less important than the quality of the vision, the relationship with the affected community, and the potential for the proposed work to contribute to meaningful systemic change. Key Qualities Voqal Partners Looks For Applicants should consider five major characteristics when assessing whether their project fits the fellowship. 1. Dream-stage or idea-stage work The idea may still be developing. Applicants do not need to present a finished initiative. What matters is having a bold vision and being ready to explore how that vision could become reality. 2. A compelling vision Voqal Partners is interested in ideas that challenge the status quo. The organization seeks approaches that can potentially disrupt systems through transformative solutions rather than simply creating small interventions that make existing systems more comfortable. 3. A path forward Having a big idea is not enough. Applicants should also demonstrate that they have some thoughts about where they could begin. This could include identifying: What they want to test What they want to learn What they want to build Which assumptions they need to explore What initial steps they could take during the fellowship The path does not need to be completely developed because the fellowship itself is intended to provide space for learning and experimentation. 4. Alignment with the fellowship Applicants should explain why the Voqal Partners Fellowship is appropriate for their idea. The application should demonstrate how the fellowship s funding, coaching, mentorship and community could help move the project forward. 5. Connection to community Applicants should be able to explain their relationship with the people most affected by the issue they are addressing. Voqal Partners places significant emphasis on community connection and the role an applicant plays in advancing the work. Fellowship Responsibilities The Voqal Partners Fellowship provides substantial freedom, but fellows are also expected to actively participate in the program. Fellows are expected to: Work on their fellowship project from April through September 2027. Attend three in-person convenings. Participate in monthly cohort calls. Engage with coaches and advisors. Share what they learned at the conclusion of the fellowship. The three convenings are scheduled for: April 2027: Opening convening July 2027: Middle convening September 2027: Closing convening Although fellows are permitted to pursue other employment or responsibilities during the fellowship, Voqal Partners asks them to make their fellowship project a priority. This flexibility may be particularly useful for applicants who have existing professional, family or community responsibilities. Do Fellows Keep Ownership of Their Ideas? Yes. Fellows retain full ownership of intellectual property developed during the fellowship. Voqal Partners does not claim ownership of a fellow s ideas, products or creations. This is an important consideration for applicants developing innovative concepts because it means the fellowship does not require fellows to surrender ownership of intellectual property created as part of their work. Can Previous Applicants Apply Again? Yes. Previous applicants are encouraged to apply again. Voqal Partners recognizes that strong ideas can evolve over time. Applying in a previous year does not prevent someone from submitting a new application or returning with an idea that has developed further. The organization also indicates that previous applications do not negatively affect future consideration. Can Previous Fellows Apply? The supplied fellowship information includes this question in the FAQ section, but does not provide a complete answer in the provided material. Applicants who have previously participated as fellows should therefore verify their eligibility directly with Voqal Partners before submitting an application. Can Fellows Have Other Jobs? Yes. Fellows are permitted to pursue other work during the fellowship. Voqal Partners recognizes that fellows may have employment, family obligations and other responsibilities. However, the organization expects the fellowship project to remain a priority throughout the program. This means applicants do not necessarily need to leave their existing employment to participate. Application Process The Voqal Partners Fellowship application is divided into four primary sections. Section 1: Eligibility The first part of the application contains questions designed to establish whether the applicant meets the fellowship s core eligibility requirements. Applicants should carefully review these requirements before investing significant time in the application. Section 2: Basic Details This section collects fundamental information about the applicant and their proposed project. Applicants may be asked for: Information about how they found the fellowship Their project name Brief project descriptions Basic personal details Section 3: The Specifics This is the central part of the application. Applicants will need to explain the future they are trying to create, how they envision moving toward that future, and what kind of support they would need from the fellowship. This section is likely to be particularly important because it gives applicants an opportunity to demonstrate the strength of their vision and their connection to the issue they are addressing. Applicants should focus on clearly communicating: The problem they are addressing Why the problem matters Their vision for change What makes their approach different What they want to explore or test What they hope to learn Why they are well positioned to pursue the idea How Voqal Partners could help Section 4: Additional Details The final section provides space for additional information. Applicants may be asked about: Their use of artificial intelligence Previous experience with coaches Additional information relevant to their application Links Supporting documents Other details they believe the selection team should know The Fellowship Budget Applicants must also submit a budget explaining how they anticipate using the $30,000 fellowship award . Importantly, Voqal Partners states that the budget is not used to evaluate the application . Instead, the budget helps the organization understand where the applicant currently stands in their planning. A budget template is provided as part of the application. Applicants should therefore use the budget to provide a realistic picture of what they believe they will need rather than attempting to create an artificially sophisticated financial plan. Application Resources Applicants can prepare for the application using resources provided by Voqal Partners, including: The application guide The fellowship question list The online application Virtual information sessions Reviewing the application guide and question list before beginning the application can help applicants understand what information they will need and organize their responses in advance. Voqal Partners Fellowship Information Sessions Voqal Partners is offering two virtual information sessions for prospective applicants. The organization states that both sessions will cover the same information, meaning applicants only need to attend one. Session 1 Date: September 18, 2026 Time: 12:00 p.m. Eastern / 9:00 a.m. Pacific Format: Virtual The first session will be recorded, with the recording expected to be shared afterward. Session 2 Date: October 14, 2026 Time: 4:00 p.m. Eastern / 1:00 p.m. Pacific Format: Virtual Applicants who cannot attend the first session can participate in the second session. 2027 Fellowship Timeline Applicants should keep the following dates in mind: Applications Open First Tuesday after Labor Day 2026 Applications Close October 31, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time Interviews January 2027 Fellows Selected February–March 2027 Opening Convening April 2027 Fellowship Programming April–September 2027 Middle Convening July 2027 Closing Convening September 2027 Because the application deadline is specific to a time zone, applicants should avoid waiting until the final day and should submit well before the stated closing time. How to Strengthen Your Voqal Partners Fellowship Application Although there is no guaranteed formula for selection, applicants can take several practical steps to make their application clearer and more compelling. Clearly explain the future you want to create Do not focus exclusively on describing what is wrong. Explain what the world, system or community could look like if your idea succeeds. Demonstrate your connection to the community Explain your relationship with the people affected by the issue. If you have lived experience, community organizing experience or another meaningful connection to the issue, make that relationship clear. Show why your idea is different Voqal Partners is interested in bold ideas that can challenge existing systems. Explain what makes your proposed approach different from conventional solutions. Be honest about what you do not know Because the fellowship is designed for early-stage ideas, applicants do not need to pretend that every detail has already been solved. Instead, identify the questions you need to answer and the assumptions you want to test. Explain what you would do with the fellowship Be specific about how the six months could help you move from an idea toward experimentation. Consider explaining: What you would investigate What you would build Who you would engage What you would test What resources you need What you hope to learn Prepare a realistic budget Even though the budget does not determine the evaluation of your application, it should demonstrate that you have thought carefully about how the fellowship resources could support your work. Use the application guide Review the official application guide and question list before submitting. This can help you understand the application structure and avoid overlooking important questions. Examples of Previous Fellows Work The fellowship has previously supported projects addressing civic participation, grassroots organizing and worker advocacy. Andrea Hart — City Bureau Andrea Hart worked on a civic newsroom model designed to train residents to report on local government and conduct community-driven investigations. The example illustrates how the fellowship can support approaches that strengthen community participation in civic life and local accountability. Erick Garcia — #GAMETHESYSTEM Erick Garcia developed a gamified approach to grassroots organizing, using digital tools to increase participation and accessibility. This demonstrates the type of experimentation that can emerge when technology and organizing are combined in unconventional ways. Rich Wallace — Equity Transformation Rich Wallace organized workers in the informal economy to pursue policy protections at city and state levels. The project demonstrates another dimension of the fellowship s focus: supporting efforts that seek structural and policy-level change for communities that may otherwise have limited access to institutional power. Why the Voqal Partners Fellowship Is Different The fellowship stands out because of its willingness to fund ideas before they have become fully established projects. Traditional funding opportunities frequently require applicants to demonstrate previous results, organizational infrastructure, detailed implementation plans or established programs. The Voqal Partners model is more focused on the person, their vision and the possibility of what their idea could become. Its approach combines: Flexible funding Personal financial support Healthcare assistance Coaching Mentorship Peer learning Community Fully funded travel Continued alumni engagement The result is an opportunity for social justice changemakers to dedicate meaningful time and resources to exploring an idea that may otherwise struggle to receive conventional funding. Who Can Apply? The fellowship is intended for social justice changemakers who meet the organization s eligibility requirements and have a bold vision for creating a more equitable future. Applicants must: Be 18 years of age or older . Be based in the United States . Be able to receive funds in the United States . Be working on an idea connected to communities in the United States. Have a social justice-oriented vision or idea. Be prepared to dedicate the fellowship period to developing and testing the idea. Be willing and able to participate in the fellowship s required activities, including the three in-person convenings. Voqal Partners does not provide visa sponsorship. The organization particularly encourages applications from people with lived experience and individuals connected to communities historically excluded from philanthropy. APPLY HERE Geographic Eligibility This is not a worldwide fellowship . The fellowship requires applicants to be based in the United States and able to receive funds in the United States . Projects may be local, regional or national in scope, but the work must focus on communities within the United States. Therefore, applicants living in countries outside the United States, including applicants from African countries such as Kenya, do not meet the stated geographic eligibility requirement unless they independently satisfy Voqal Partners U.S.-based eligibility requirements. Important Deadline The application deadline for the Voqal Partners Fellowship 2027 is October 31, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time . Applicants should not wait until the final hours to submit their application. Technical problems, incomplete responses or missing documents can create unnecessary difficulties close to the deadline. A good strategy is to complete the application ahead of time, review every response, check the budget and submit before the final day. How to Apply Interested applicants should use the official Voqal Partners application portal to begin their application. Before applying, prospective fellows should also review the official application guide and question list so they understand what is expected. Applicants who have questions can contact Voqal Partners through fellowship@voqalpartners.org . Visit HERE to learn more about the Voqal Partners Fellowship 2027. Frequently Asked Questions Is the Voqal Partners Fellowship fully funded? The fellowship provides a $30,000 award, a $1,000 healthcare stipend and covers travel costs associated with the three required in-person convenings. Childcare support is also available for fellows with dependents under 18. Do I need an established organization to apply? No. The fellowship specifically welcomes dream-stage and idea-stage work. Applicants do not need a finished organization, product, campaign or business plan. Can I use the $30,000 for living expenses? Yes. The funding has no stated restrictions on how fellows use the award, provided the expenses support the fellow and their work. This can include living expenses, equipment, contractors, travel and implementation costs. Do I keep ownership of my intellectual property? Yes. Fellows retain ownership of intellectual property developed during the fellowship. Can I work another job during the fellowship? Yes. Other work is permitted, although fellows are expected to prioritize their fellowship project. How many fellows are selected? Voqal Partners selects eight fellows each year . Are previous applicants allowed to apply? Yes. Previous applicants are encouraged to apply again. Does Voqal Partners sponsor visas? No. The organization does not offer visa sponsorship. Must I attend the in-person convenings? Yes. Attendance at all three convenings is a core part of the fellowship experience. What happens to my application information? Voqal Partners states that applications are reviewed by a select group of community members, including program alumni, staff and partners. Access is limited to the evaluation period, and the organization states that it will not share applicants ideas or details beyond this process without their knowledge. Conclusion The Voqal Partners Fellowship 2027 offers a distinctive opportunity for social justice changemakers who have ambitious ideas but may not yet have the organizational infrastructure, funding or resources needed to turn those ideas into reality. With $30,000 in flexible funding , a $1,000 healthcare stipend , coaching and mentorship, peer support, fully funded travel to three convenings and access to an alumni community, the fellowship is designed to give selected changemakers the time and resources to explore, test and develop new approaches to systemic change. The opportunity is particularly relevant to people with lived experience and strong connections to the communities they serve, especially individuals from groups historically excluded from traditional philanthropy. However, prospective applicants should pay close attention to the geographic requirement. The fellowship is U.S.-based , applicants must be 18 or older, based in the United States and able to receive funds in the U.S. , and Voqal Partners does not provide visa sponsorship. For eligible applicants with a bold social justice idea, the October 31, 2026 deadline provides an important opportunity to seek support for an idea that may be too early or unconventional for traditional funding programs. Applicants should begin by reviewing the application guide and question list, developing a clear explanation of the future they want to create, identifying what they want to test or learn during the six-month fellowship, and preparing a realistic budget for the $30,000 award. title: British Academy Elevate Programme Leadership Stream: Apply for an Intensive Leadership Development Programme for Early Career Researchers
summary: The British Academy Elevate Programme – Leadership Stream is an intensive, CPD-accredited professional development programme designed to help Early Career Researchers (ECRs) develop the leadership skills, confidence, networks and practical experience needed to progress in academia and beyond. Delivered by the British Academy , the UK’s national academy for the humanities and social sciences, the Elevate Programme combines structured leadership training with mentoring, coaching, networking and practical opportunities to apply newly acquired skills. The programme is particularly suited to Early Career Researchers in SHAPE disciplines who are preparing to take on leadership responsibilities or are already moving into leadership positions. The programme is highly selective, with approximately 62 participants selected each year from the British Academy Early Career Researcher Network and Wellcome-funded researchers. The annual programme normally runs from March to June , while applications open in September . Participants take part in a combination of online and in-person activities, depending on where they are based. What Is the British Academy Elevate Programme – Leadership Stream? The British Academy Elevate Programme—Leadership Stream is a structured leadership development initiative created specifically for Early Career Researchers. Rather than focusing exclusively on academic research skills, the programme addresses the broader professional capabilities researchers need to become effective leaders. These include communication, strategic planning, research management, collaboration, influencing decision-making, and managing teams and projects. The programme recognises that leadership opportunities can arise at different stages of an academic or research career. As a result, it is designed to be adaptable to researchers at early, mid and later stages of their early-career journey. Participants are supported through a combination of: Leadership training Interactive workshops Professional mentoring Individual and group coaching Peer networking Practical leadership activities Opportunities to apply leadership skills in professional settings Post-programme engagement with the wider Early Career Researcher Network The programme therefore provides participants with both theoretical understanding and practical experience that can be applied directly to their research, academic, professional or organisational responsibilities. Key Features of the British Academy Elevate Leadership Programme The Elevate Programme is designed around several interconnected elements of professional development. 1. Intensive leadership training Participants receive structured training focused on developing the skills required to become effective leaders. The training can help researchers understand how to: Lead projects effectively Manage teams and responsibilities Communicate with different audiences Influence decision-making Develop strategic approaches to their work Navigate professional challenges Build productive collaborations Manage research-related activities Drive positive change within organisations and institutions The emphasis is on practical leadership rather than leadership theory alone. 2. Interactive workshops The programme includes interactive workshops that allow participants to explore leadership concepts and apply them to real professional situations. These workshops provide opportunities for participants to learn from facilitators and fellow researchers while considering how leadership principles can be used in their own careers. The interactive format can also help participants develop confidence in areas such as communication, teamwork, problem-solving and strategic thinking. 3. Mentoring Mentoring forms an important component of the programme. Through mentoring, participants can benefit from guidance, experience and perspectives that can help them navigate their career development and leadership responsibilities. Mentoring can be particularly valuable for Early Career Researchers who are preparing to transition into positions where they need to coordinate people, manage projects, influence stakeholders or take greater responsibility for research and organisational outcomes. 4. Coaching Participants also receive coaching as part of the programme. Coaching provides an opportunity to reflect on individual leadership strengths, challenges and development areas. It can help researchers identify practical approaches for becoming more effective in their professional roles. This combination of training, mentoring and coaching gives participants multiple forms of support throughout the programme. 5. Peer networking The programme brings together a selective group of Early Career Researchers, creating opportunities for participants to develop professional relationships with peers. Networking can enable participants to: Exchange ideas and experiences Learn from researchers working in different areas Develop professional connections Identify potential collaborators Share approaches to common leadership challenges Build relationships that can continue beyond the programme The peer network is an important part of the wider professional development experience offered by Elevate. What Skills Will Participants Develop? The British Academy Elevate Programme is designed to develop a broad range of leadership and professional competencies. Participants will have the opportunity to strengthen their ability to: Lead projects and initiatives Researchers often become responsible for projects involving multiple people, institutions or stakeholders. The programme helps participants develop the leadership capabilities required to coordinate such activities effectively. Manage teams Effective leadership requires more than technical expertise. Researchers stepping into leadership roles may need to delegate responsibilities, support colleagues, manage expectations and foster productive working relationships. The programme provides training relevant to these responsibilities. Communicate effectively Communication is a central component of leadership. Participants develop practical knowledge that can help them communicate ideas, expectations, strategies and decisions more effectively. Influence decision-making Researchers increasingly need to communicate their evidence and expertise to decision-makers both inside and outside academia. The Elevate Programme helps participants build confidence and skills for influencing decisions and engaging with different stakeholders. Develop strategic thinking Strategic planning is another important component of effective leadership. Participants gain practical knowledge that can help them think beyond individual tasks and consider broader objectives, priorities, resources and long-term outcomes. Manage research effectively The programme also supports researchers in developing skills related to research management. This can be particularly valuable for researchers who are beginning to coordinate larger projects, work with teams or take responsibility for complex research activities. Navigate professional challenges Leadership often involves dealing with uncertainty, competing priorities, difficult decisions and unexpected challenges. Through training, coaching and peer learning, participants can develop greater confidence in navigating these situations. Foster collaboration Modern research frequently depends on collaboration across disciplines, organisations and professional networks. The programme supports participants in developing collaborative approaches and building relationships that can contribute to stronger professional and research outcomes. Who Can Benefit From the Programme? The British Academy Elevate Leadership Stream is designed for Early Career Researchers, particularly those working in SHAPE disciplines . SHAPE refers broadly to disciplines within the social sciences, humanities and related areas, covering fields where researchers study people, societies, cultures, economies, institutions and human behaviour. The programme can be relevant to researchers who are: Preparing to move into leadership roles Already taking on leadership responsibilities Managing or contributing to research projects Interested in developing their professional leadership capabilities Seeking to strengthen their communication and strategic planning skills Interested in research management Looking to expand their professional networks Considering leadership opportunities within or beyond academia Importantly, the programme is adaptable to different stages of the early-career journey. A Programme Designed for Leadership Inside and Outside Academia One of the strengths of the Elevate Leadership Stream is that its benefits are not restricted to traditional academic career pathways. The leadership skills developed through the programme can potentially be applied in areas such as: Academic leadership Research management Policy engagement Organisational leadership Professional services Public engagement Research funding and stakeholder engagement Mentoring and skills development Leadership positions outside academia This broader focus makes the programme relevant to researchers who want to translate their research and professional expertise into wider societal and organisational impact. Delivery Format of the British Academy Elevate Programme The programme uses a combination of online and face-to-face learning. Participants can expect a mixture of: Online workshops In-person workshops Specialised training sessions Mentoring Coaching Networking events Practical post-programme activities In-person participation for UK-based researchers Researchers based in the UK should be prepared for approximately 10 in-person training sessions . Each in-person session lasts approximately one to two days and takes place at a different location in the UK. Consequently, UK-based participants should be prepared to travel to the various locations where the training sessions are held. This means applicants should consider the time and travel commitment involved before applying. Online participation for researchers outside the UK Online delivery is available to participants who are based outside the UK . This provides an important opportunity for eligible researchers located internationally to participate without having to attend the UK-based in-person training sessions. Post-Programme Responsibilities Participation in the Elevate Programme does not end when the formal training sessions are completed. Within nine months of completing the programme , participants are required to organise an event or activity for the Early Career Researcher Network. The British Academy provides funding support for this activity. Participants must also provide peer-to-peer mentoring to the next cohort as part of the programme s post-programme requirements. These responsibilities provide participants with an opportunity to put their leadership training into practice. Instead of simply receiving training, participants are expected to demonstrate leadership by organising an activity and supporting other Early Career Researchers. Professional Recognition Through CPD Accreditation The British Academy Elevate Programme – Leadership Stream is CPD-accredited . Continuing Professional Development, commonly referred to as CPD, provides a structured way of demonstrating ongoing learning and professional development. For participants, CPD accreditation adds professional recognition to the leadership training received through the programme. This can be valuable when demonstrating professional development to: Employers Research institutions Academic institutions Funders Professional organisations Potential collaborators The accreditation can also strengthen a participant s professional profile by providing evidence of structured leadership development. GetTWOit Skills Passport and Micro-Credentials Participants in the British Academy Elevate Programme can also receive a GetTWOit Skills Passport documenting the skills acquired through the programme. A Skills Passport is provided for each completed training session, creating a structured record of the professional skills developed. This can help participants demonstrate specific competencies rather than simply stating that they attended a leadership programme. The Skills Passport functions as a form of micro-credential and can provide additional evidence of professional learning. Skills Passport after the Network event Participants can also receive a GetTWOit Skills Passport after organising an event for the Early Career Researcher Network. This additional credential can demonstrate the participant s ability to take the leadership training they received and use it to develop or deliver learning activities for other Early Career Researchers. It therefore provides evidence not only of participation in training but also of practical leadership and knowledge-sharing. How the Programme Can Strengthen Your CV Professional development programmes can be particularly useful for researchers who are building their academic or professional profiles. The British Academy Elevate Programme offers several elements that can contribute to a stronger CV. Participants can potentially demonstrate: Completion of CPD-accredited leadership training Leadership development Project management capabilities Team management skills Strategic planning experience Communication skills Research management experience Networking and collaboration Mentoring experience Event or activity organisation Peer-to-peer knowledge sharing Practical application of leadership skills The programme is therefore structured to provide tangible evidence of professional development that can be communicated to employers and funders. Why Leadership Skills Matter for Early Career Researchers Research careers increasingly require researchers to operate beyond the boundaries of individual research projects. As researchers progress, they may be expected to manage teams, coordinate projects, communicate findings to different audiences, collaborate across institutions, secure funding, engage policymakers or contribute to organisational strategy. Technical research expertise remains essential, but leadership and interpersonal skills can also play a significant role in career progression. The Elevate Programme addresses this broader professional development need by combining research-sector knowledge with leadership development. Networking and Long-Term Professional Development Another important aspect of the programme is the opportunity to become part of a community of Early Career Researchers. Participants can develop relationships with other researchers who are facing similar career-development questions and leadership challenges. These connections can potentially support: Future research collaborations Knowledge exchange Professional mentoring Cross-disciplinary relationships Career advice Leadership development Peer learning Engagement with the wider research community The requirement to mentor a subsequent cohort further strengthens the programme s emphasis on creating a continuing professional network rather than a one-time training experience. Application Timeline The British Academy Elevate Programme is offered annually. According to the programme information: Applications open: September Programme delivery: March to June Selection: Competitive and application-based Annual cohort: Approximately 62 participants Application deadline The information provided for this article does not specify a closing date for applications . Applicants should therefore consult the official British Academy application page for the current application deadline and any updated dates before submitting an application. How to Apply for the British Academy Elevate Programme Applications are submitted through the British Academy s application process for the Elevate Programme – Leadership Stream. Applicants should carefully review the programme s dedicated How to Apply information before beginning their application. A strong application should clearly demonstrate why leadership development is relevant to the applicant s current career stage and professional goals. Applicants should consider explaining: Their Early Career Researcher background. Their research area and connection to the relevant disciplines. Their current or anticipated leadership responsibilities. The leadership skills they want to develop. How the programme fits into their career development. How they expect to apply the skills gained through Elevate. Their interest in collaboration and peer learning. Their ability to participate fully in the programme. Their readiness to undertake the post-programme responsibilities. Applicants should also carefully check the official eligibility requirements because programme requirements and application details may be updated for each annual cohort. APPLY HERE Tips for Preparing a Strong Application 1. Clearly explain your leadership potential Do not focus only on your academic achievements. Show how you have demonstrated initiative, responsibility, collaboration or leadership. 2. Connect the programme to your career goals Explain why leadership development is important at your current stage and what you intend to accomplish with the skills gained. 3. Demonstrate practical experience Examples of managing projects, coordinating activities, supervising people, organising events, collaborating with stakeholders or mentoring colleagues can help demonstrate leadership potential. 4. Show how you will contribute to the cohort The programme is also about peer networking and learning. Explain how your experience and perspective could contribute to the wider cohort. 5. Consider the programme commitment UK-based applicants should take into account the requirement to attend approximately ten in-person training sessions at different UK locations. title: WFP Ethics Officer P-3 in Rome, Italy: International Professional Job in Ethics, Compliance and Risk Management
summary: The United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) is inviting applications for an Ethics Officer – P-3 position based at its headquarters in Rome, Italy . This is a full-time International Professional opportunity for an experienced ethics, compliance, legal, risk management or international affairs professional seeking to contribute to ethical governance and accountability within one of the world s largest humanitarian organizations. The position is located in the WFP Ethics Office and reports to the Senior Ethics Officer . The successful candidate will help strengthen WFP s ethical framework by advising employees and management, supporting conflict-of-interest disclosure processes, contributing to ethics-related policies, supporting protection against retaliation, developing training programmes, and strengthening relationships across WFP and the wider United Nations system. The application deadline is 29 September 2026 at 23:59 Central European Time (Rome) . WFP Ethics Officer P-3 Job at a Glance Opportunity Details Job title Ethics Officer – P-3 Organization World Food Programme (WFP) Job type International Professional Grade P-3 Job requisition JR126545 Location Rome, Italy Work arrangement Fully present/on-site Working hours Full time Contract Fixed-term, with a one-year probationary period Application deadline 29 September 2026, 23:59 CET Nationality Open to candidates of all nationalities Education Advanced university degree in a relevant field Experience At least 5 years of relevant progressively responsible experience Languages English at C level plus intermediate knowledge of a second official UN language Application documents CV and cover letter at the application stage WFP s official careers information describes P-3 positions as professional roles involving specialized and analytical responsibilities, with the complexity of responsibilities increasing with grade. International Professional positions generally operate under internationally determined compensation and benefits arrangements. About the World Food Programme The World Food Programme is the world s largest humanitarian organization. Its work focuses on saving lives during emergencies while using food assistance to support pathways toward peace, stability and prosperity for people affected by conflict, disasters and climate-related impacts. WFP operates through a large international workforce and a network of country, regional and headquarters offices. Its careers framework emphasizes meaningful work, continuous professional development and a multicultural working environment. WFP also places strong emphasis on integrity, collaboration, commitment, humanity and inclusion. These values are particularly relevant to an Ethics Officer because the position contributes directly to maintaining trust, accountability and responsible conduct across the organization. What Is the WFP Ethics Office? The Ethics Office plays an important role in helping WFP maintain high standards of integrity and ethical conduct. According to WFP, the Ethics Office is an independent and formal office that assists the Executive Director in nurturing a culture of ethics throughout the organization. It helps employees think through ethical dilemmas, understand relevant rules and policies, and raise concerns without fear of retaliation. The office s work includes several interconnected areas: Ethics advice and guidance Training, education and outreach Protection against retaliation Conflicts of interest and financial disclosures Ethical standards in policies and organizational practices Anti-fraud and anti-corruption principles Confidentiality and data protection considerations United Nations ethics coordination Support for ethical decision-making The WFP Code of Conduct reflects principles including human rights, social justice, dignity, equal rights, competence, integrity, impartiality and discretion. It also addresses areas such as anti-fraud and anti-corruption and protection against sexual exploitation and abuse. About the Ethics Officer – P-3 Position The Ethics Officer will work within the Ethics Office at WFP headquarters in Rome and report to the Senior Ethics Officer . The central purpose of the position is to support the development and maintenance of a robust ethical framework within WFP. This means the role is not limited to reviewing rules or responding to individual questions. It combines ethics advisory work, policy analysis, conflict-of-interest management, retaliation protection, training, communication, reporting and stakeholder engagement . The role therefore requires someone who can combine technical knowledge with strong interpersonal skills, discretion, independence and the ability to communicate sensitive issues clearly. Key Responsibilities of the Ethics Officer 1. Support the Ethics Office Strategy and Work Plan The Ethics Officer will provide substantive input into the definition and implementation of the Ethics Office s strategy and work plan. This involves helping determine priorities, activities and approaches that strengthen ethical standards across WFP. The role therefore requires an understanding of how ethics functions can be translated into practical organizational systems rather than treated simply as theoretical principles. 2. Provide Ethics Advice and Guidance A major part of the position involves providing timely advice and guidance to WFP employees and management on ethics and standards of conduct. The officer will also be responsible for properly tracking and recording ethics-related queries. This requires the ability to: Understand complex ethical situations Identify relevant policies and standards Provide clear and balanced advice Maintain confidentiality Exercise independent judgment Communicate effectively with different stakeholders Document advice and follow-up appropriately The importance of this function is reflected in the broader work of WFP s Ethics Office. Its 2025 annual report recorded 890 requests for ethics advice and guidance , with 96 percent of respondents to voluntary satisfaction surveys reporting that they were satisfied or very satisfied with the advice received and its timeliness. 3. Support the Annual Conflict-of-Interest Disclosure Programme The Ethics Officer will contribute to the management of WFP s annual disclosure programme. This includes reviewing disclosed conflicts of interest, providing advice and helping ensure the programme operates smoothly. Conflict-of-interest management is an important part of organizational integrity because employees may sometimes have private interests or outside activities that could conflict with their official responsibilities. WFP s Ethics Office explains that its annual disclosure programme is designed to identify and address such conflicts through disclosures involving assets, liabilities, investments and outside activities for certain categories of employees. For the Ethics Officer, this means applying ethical judgment to real situations and helping employees and management understand how potential conflicts should be identified and addressed. 4. Develop Ethics Training and Learning Programmes The successful candidate will help develop and deliver: Ethics training programmes E-learning modules Train-the-trainer programmes Sessions on WFP values Training on ethical principles Training on standards of conduct This responsibility requires more than technical knowledge. The Ethics Officer must also be able to explain complex concepts to employees with different professional and cultural backgrounds. WFP emphasizes training and outreach as important components of building an ethical culture because employees need to understand the values, standards and principles expected of them. 5. Advise on Ethics-Related Policies and Regulations The Ethics Officer will provide advice and review when WFP develops or updates: Policies Circulars Regulations Other organizational documents involving ethical considerations The officer may also be requested by other departments to provide ethics advice during policy development. This makes policy analysis an important component of the role. The successful candidate must therefore be comfortable reading complex institutional documents, identifying ethical implications and communicating recommendations clearly. 6. Support Protection Against Retaliation Another major responsibility involves supporting the review of requests for protection against retaliation. The officer may contribute to: Reviewing retaliation-protection requests Preparing memoranda Drafting responses to complainants Assessing relevant circumstances Applying whistleblower protection policies Maintaining confidentiality Supporting individuals who raise concerns WFP states that its Whistleblower Protection Policy is designed to protect employees from retaliation when they engage in protected activities, and that the protection applies to current and former employees regardless of contract type or duration. This is a particularly sensitive area of the position and requires independence, impartiality, careful listening and sound judgment. 7. Strengthen the Visibility of the Ethics Office The Ethics Officer will also contribute to enhancing the presence of the Ethics Office through: WFP internal websites External websites Online communication channels Relevant publications Other communication platforms This responsibility shows that the role also has a communication component. Ethics policies are most effective when employees understand them and know where to seek advice. Therefore, communicating the work of the Ethics Office clearly is part of strengthening an organization s ethical culture. 8. Support Reporting and Analysis The position will involve preparing analysis, drafting material and supporting reporting on the overall work of the Ethics Office. The officer may therefore need to translate complex information into: Reports Briefings Memos Analytical documents Policy notes Communication materials Strong analytical and writing abilities are consequently important. 9. Build Internal and External Relationships The Ethics Officer will build positive and effective relationships both within WFP and outside the organization. External cooperation may include engagement across: The United Nations system Other UN entities Rome-based UN agencies Professional ethics networks Relevant institutional partners WFP s Ethics Office already works to promote coherence across the United Nations system, including through cooperation with other ethics offices and Rome-based agencies. The successful candidate will therefore need strong interpersonal and partnership-building abilities. 10. Perform Other Duties as Assigned The officer may also undertake other responsibilities assigned by the Senior Ethics Officer when necessary to support the mandate of the Ethics Office and strengthen ethics and accountability across WFP. Minimum Education Requirements Applicants must have an advanced university degree in one of the following areas or a closely related discipline: Law Ethics Public administration International affairs Compliance Another related field This educational requirement makes the position particularly relevant to professionals with postgraduate qualifications in legal, governance, ethics, international policy or compliance-related disciplines. An advanced degree is important because the position requires the ability to interpret policies and regulations, assess ethical risks, advise senior stakeholders and prepare sophisticated written analysis. Professional Experience Required Candidates must have at least five years of relevant progressively responsible professional experience . The experience should be connected to areas such as: Legal advice Compliance Risk assessment Ethics Related professional fields The phrase progressively responsible is important. The position is not intended primarily for someone who has only completed an academic programme or gained limited entry-level experience. Candidates should be able to demonstrate increasing responsibility and professional judgment in their previous roles. Relevant experience could involve advising organizations, reviewing compliance risks, developing policies, supporting investigations or whistleblower systems, providing ethics guidance, drafting legal or policy documents, or managing institutional risk. Knowledge and Skills Required The position requires a combination of technical, analytical and interpersonal skills. Understanding of Ethics, Compliance and Risk Candidates should have a theoretical understanding of: Ethics Compliance Risk assessment Standards of conduct Ethical decision-making The successful candidate must be able to apply this knowledge to practical organizational situations. Advisory Skills The Ethics Officer will advise a wide range of stakeholders on different ethical issues. This means applicants should be comfortable communicating with people at different levels of an international organization. Whistleblower Protection Knowledge Candidates must have technical knowledge of whistleblower protection policies. They should also demonstrate the ability to prepare: Legal memoranda Notes to file Analytical documents Written responses This is particularly relevant to the retaliation-protection component of the position. Independence and Impartiality Because the Ethics Office performs an independent and confidential function, the Ethics Officer must act with: Integrity Independence Impartiality Professional discretion The successful candidate must be able to provide objective advice even when dealing with sensitive or difficult situations. Interpersonal Skills WFP works with people from diverse professional, national and cultural backgrounds. The Ethics Officer must therefore be able to establish respectful working relationships and communicate effectively with colleagues from different backgrounds. Training and Facilitation Skills Applicants should demonstrate the ability to deliver training to small and medium-sized audiences. This is important because the role includes developing and facilitating ethics learning programmes. Active Listening The position specifically requires the ability to listen attentively to people seeking advice or protection from retaliation. This is particularly important because ethics-related cases may involve sensitive professional circumstances. Language Requirements The position requires: English: Fluency at Level C . In addition, candidates need intermediate knowledge at Level B of a second official United Nations language . The listed languages include: Arabic Chinese French Russian Spanish Portuguese This language requirement is particularly relevant to the international nature of the role. Candidates should therefore carefully assess their language proficiency before applying. Who Can Apply? The position is classified as an International Professional role and is open to candidates of all nationalities . This is an important distinction because the position is not restricted to Italian citizens or citizens of a particular region. Qualified professionals can therefore come from any country or continent, provided they meet the professional, academic and language requirements. WFP also explicitly states that it is committed to equal employment opportunity and encourages qualified candidates to apply regardless of: Race Colour National origin Ethnic background Social background Genetic information Gender Gender identity or expression Sexual orientation Religion or belief HIV status Disability Therefore, there is no race or ethnicity restriction attached to the position. However, being eligible to apply does not mean that an applicant will automatically be selected. Candidates must still meet the position s education, experience, skills and language requirements and successfully complete WFP s recruitment process. Location: Rome, Italy The position is based at WFP headquarters in Rome, Italy , within the Ethics Office. The vacancy is classified as fully present , meaning the selected candidate is expected to work from the designated workplace rather than remotely. The selected candidate will be required to relocate to Rome to take up the assignment. This is therefore an important consideration for candidates currently living outside Italy. This means that, under the conditions stated in the vacancy announcement, the incumbent is not subject to WFP s regular reassignment process unless the position is later reclassified as rotational. WFP explains that International Professional positions generally involve specialized and analytical work, with compensation and benefits determined according to applicable international civil service arrangements. The listed benefits include: Basic salary Post adjustment Relocation entitlement Visa support Travel allowances Shipment allowances 30 days of annual leave Home leave Education grant for dependent children Pension plan Medical insurance These benefits are particularly relevant to international candidates who may need to relocate to Italy for the assignment. Applicants should note that the precise compensation package depends on the applicable terms and conditions of the appointment. Why Work for WFP? Meaningful humanitarian work WFP s work directly supports people affected by emergencies, conflict, disasters and climate-related challenges. International working environment WFP operates with a highly multicultural workforce, creating opportunities to work alongside professionals from different countries and backgrounds. Professional development WFP invests in employee development through training, accreditation, coaching, mentorship and internal mobility opportunities. International career opportunities A career with WFP can potentially provide opportunities to work across country, regional and global offices. Why the Ethics Officer Role Matters to WFP Ethics may sometimes be viewed as an administrative function, but within a large humanitarian organization, it is closely connected to institutional credibility and operational effectiveness. WFP works in complex environments and handles significant responsibilities involving humanitarian assistance, partnerships, resources and people. Maintaining public and internal trust therefore requires strong standards of conduct and accountability. The report emphasizes the importance of safeguarding WFP s reputation and credibility and describes the Ethics Office as playing a vital role in providing timely guidance and supporting risk management. The Ethics Officer therefore contributes to an important institutional function: helping employees make sound ethical decisions and helping WFP maintain confidence in its operations. Examples of Ethics Work at WFP The broader work of the Ethics Office provides useful context for understanding this position. Ethics advice and guidance Employees can seek confidential advice when facing ethical questions or risks. These functions closely correspond to the responsibilities outlined for the Ethics Officer position. Emphasize experience involving: Ethics Legal advisory work Compliance Risk assessment Whistleblower protection Policy development Governance Organizational accountability Training Investigations or related advisory functions International organizations Public administration 2. Applicants should show how their responsibilities have developed over time. Your application should therefore demonstrate experience in drafting or reviewing: Policies Legal memoranda Regulatory documents Internal guidance Advisory notes Risk assessments Compliance documents 5. Demonstrate training experience If you have delivered professional training, workshops, seminars or awareness sessions, highlight this clearly.
