title: Swiss Fellowship for Inclusive Development 2027 at AUC: Graduate Diploma Tuition Funding in Public Policy and Public Administration
summary: The American University in Cairo is inviting eligible graduate applicants to consider the Swiss Fellowship for Inclusive Development, commonly abbreviated as SFID. Designed for academically strong students, the opportunity provides substantial tuition and fee support for graduate-diploma study in public policy or public administration at AUC. The credits completed through either diploma can also count toward the university’s Master of Public Policy or Master of Public Administration degree. This makes the Swiss Fellowship for Inclusive Development at AUC particularly relevant to applicants who want advanced training in public policy, governance, public administration, institutional development, or related public-service fields. In addition to academic study, recipients undertake a structured weekly work commitment with AUC’s Public Policy HUB, connecting their coursework with policy research and practical engagement. The fellowship is not open to every international applicant. AUC limits eligibility to Egyptian nationals and certain refugees residing in Egypt. Applicants must also meet the university’s graduate admission requirements and demonstrate an excellent academic record. Prospective candidates should therefore check both their nationality or refugee eligibility and their academic readiness before beginning the two-part application process. Swiss Fellowship for Inclusive Development at a Glance Detail Information Host institution The American University in Cairo, Egypt Official name Swiss Fellowship for Inclusive Development (SFID) Supported study Graduate Diploma in Public Policy or Graduate Diploma in Public Administration Future academic pathway Diploma credits can count toward an MPP or MPA at AUC Duration Two semesters, subject to a satisfactory review after the first semester Tuition coverage Up to nine credits per semester Additional covered fees Student services and activities fees; medical service and health insurance fees Study status Full-time enrollment is required Academic standard while funded Minimum cumulative GPA of 3.2 Practical commitment At least 12 working hours each week with the Public Policy HUB Next application deadline November 2, 2026, for the Spring 2027 fellowship cycle Official information AUC Swiss Fellowship for Inclusive Development page What Is the Swiss Fellowship for Inclusive Development? The Swiss Fellowship for Inclusive Development is an AUC graduate funding opportunity for new students with excellent academic performance. Its central purpose is to cover the credit hours required for an eligible graduate diploma in public policy or public administration. AUC explains that the same credits can subsequently count toward the Master of Public Policy or Master of Public Administration, allowing the diploma to function as a meaningful step toward a related master’s degree rather than as an isolated short course. The structure combines three important elements: Graduate-level academic training: Recipients enroll full-time in one of the two approved graduate-diploma programs. Financial support: The award covers tuition for a maximum of nine credits per semester and several mandatory university and health-related fees. Applied policy experience: Fellows contribute at least 12 working hours per week to AUC’s Public Policy HUB. The Public Policy HUB was created within AUC’s School of Global Affairs and Public Policy to help develop, test, refine, and communicate responses to public-policy challenges. It brings policy scholars and mentors together with emerging policy analysts and supports the production of policy research and briefs. Consequently, the weekly work requirement is a substantive part of the experience rather than a purely administrative condition. It can expose fellows to the process of turning policy ideas into structured analysis intended for policymakers and the wider public. More information about this initiative is available on the official Public Policy HUB page . Eligible Graduate Programs and Degree Pathways The fellowship is tied specifically to full-time study in one of the following AUC programs: Graduate Diploma in Public Policy Graduate Diploma in Public Administration Applicants should not assume that the award can be transferred to an unrelated graduate program. The official fellowship terms identify only these two diploma routes. An important feature is the relationship between the diplomas and AUC’s related master’s degrees. Credits earned while completing the Graduate Diploma in Public Policy can count toward the Master of Public Policy, while credits from the Graduate Diploma in Public Administration can count toward the Master of Public Administration. This arrangement may benefit candidates who want to build graduate credentials progressively, beginning with a diploma and later continuing toward a master’s degree. However, fellowship coverage is limited to the stated two-semester award and the eligible diploma credit hours. The fact that credits can count toward a later master’s degree does not mean that the fellowship automatically finances the remainder of an MPP or MPA. Applicants planning to continue should separately investigate the academic transition requirements, remaining degree credits, future tuition, and any other funding opportunities. Financial Coverage and Benefits AUC lists the following costs as covered by the Swiss Fellowship for Inclusive Development: Tuition fees for up to nine credits per semester. Across the stated two-semester duration, this represents coverage of as many as 18 credits in total, provided the recipient remains eligible after the first-semester review. Student services and activities fees. These are university fees connected with the services and activities available to enrolled students. Medical service and health insurance fees. The award covers the health-related fees specifically named in the official terms. The phrase “full coverage” on the AUC fellowship page refers to the credit hours needed to complete the eligible graduate diploma, within the maximum of nine funded credits per semester. Applicants should read that wording together with the detailed award list. The official page does not list a living allowance, monthly stipend, accommodation, meals, books, equipment, local transportation, visa costs, relocation expenses, or international travel as covered benefits. Candidates should not budget on the assumption that these unlisted costs will be paid. This distinction matters. The award offers strong academic-cost support, but it should not be described as an all-expenses-paid package unless AUC later publishes additional coverage in an individual award letter or updated terms. Applicants should prepare a personal budget for any expenses not expressly included and seek written clarification from AUC when necessary. Fellowship Duration and Continuation Conditions The award lasts for two semesters. Continued funding for the second semester is not unconditional: AUC reviews the fellow’s academic performance after the first semester and requires satisfactory progress. To retain the award, a recipient must maintain a minimum GPA of 3.2. This academic threshold should be treated as an ongoing condition, not simply an entry qualification. A fellow whose performance falls below the stated minimum may risk losing continued support. Recipients must also remain full-time students in the approved public policy or public administration graduate-diploma program and complete the required Public Policy HUB work. Because the academic and work obligations run together, candidates should assess whether they can realistically manage a full-time graduate course load alongside at least 12 working hours every week. Who Can Apply? The official eligibility rules identify two nationality or status groups: Egyptian nationals Refugees residing in Egypt who are Yemeni, Palestinian, Syrian, or Sudanese applicants The wording is specific. It does not announce eligibility for all nationalities, all refugees, all residents of Egypt, or all applicants from Africa or the Middle East. A refugee applicant must both reside in Egypt and fall within one of the four nationality groups named by AUC. The fellowship is intended for new graduate degree-seeking students who satisfy AUC’s full graduate admission requirements. AUC also refers to continuing students in the context of retaining the award and maintaining the required GPA. Prospective applicants should therefore understand the primary applicant profile as a new graduate student seeking admission, while the continuation rule governs recipients after the award begins. Academic and Admission Qualifications Fellowship eligibility and admission to AUC are connected but distinct. A candidate must be admissible to the relevant graduate program, and an admission offer does not by itself guarantee fellowship selection. At university level, AUC states that graduate applicants must hold an accredited bachelor’s degree and have an academic record sufficient for full or provisional admission. A specific department may impose additional or higher standards. Credentials must be submitted in English; documents issued in another language must be accompanied by an official English translation. For master’s and graduate-diploma admission consideration, AUC’s current general checklist includes: A completed online graduate application. Payment of the application fee online. Selection of up to two graduate programs for admission processing. A statement of purpose of approximately 500 words for each program selected, explaining the applicant’s interest, relevant skills or experience, and long-term academic and professional objectives. An updated curriculum vitae showing education and any work experience. At least two online recommendation letters from people familiar with the applicant’s academic or professional background. Official academic records, including the final detailed bachelor’s transcript and proof that the degree was completed. Depending on the case, an enrollment certificate or an equivalency certificate from Egypt’s Supreme Council of Universities may also be requested. Satisfactory English-language proficiency results. AUC notes that accepted tests can include the TOEFL iBT, Academic IELTS, and specified Cambridge English examinations, while individual programs may require higher scores. A clear valid national identity card for Egyptian applicants, or the information pages of a passport for international applicants and Egyptian dual nationals. One recent passport-size photograph in electronic form. Any additional requirements imposed by the selected program or requested for an individual case. Applicants should use the official AUC graduate admissions page as the controlling source for the complete and most current checklist. They should also review the selected diploma’s program-specific requirements before submission. A strong academic record is particularly important because the fellowship description expressly targets new graduate students with excellent academic performance. Responsibilities of Selected Fellows Receiving the award creates continuing obligations. According to AUC, every fellow must: Enroll full-time in the Graduate Diploma in Public Policy or Graduate Diploma in Public Administration. Maintain a GPA of at least 3.2. Complete a minimum of 12 working hours per week with the Public Policy HUB. Respond to reporting requests from AUC by the deadlines communicated by the university. Supply requested materials that may include photographs or information about academic progress for reporting purposes. Attend fellowship meetings or events when requested by the relevant university units. Candidates should consider these conditions before applying. The 12-hour weekly commitment is substantial, particularly when combined with full-time graduate study. It may provide valuable policy experience, but it also requires dependable scheduling, professional conduct, timely communication, and consistent academic performance. Application Deadline for Spring and Fall 2027 The nearest published deadline is for the Spring 2027 fellowship cycle : Application opens: October 7, 2026 Application deadline: November 2, 2026 AUC also publishes two application cycles for Fall 2027 : Cycle 1 opens: December 22, 2026 Cycle 1 deadline: January 17, 2027 Cycle 2 opens: April 6, 2027 Cycle 2 deadline: May 6, 2027 These dates come from AUC’s fellowship deadline page, which was last updated on August 23, 2026. Applicants should recheck the official AUC fellowship deadlines immediately before submitting because universities may revise application calendars. The dates above concern the fellowship application cycle. Because AUC requires applicants to submit a graduate admission application as well as a fellowship application, candidates must also comply with any admission deadline applicable to their intended semester. Do not assume that finishing one form automatically completes the other process. How to Apply for the Swiss Fellowship for Inclusive Development AUC describes a two-step application process. Both steps are essential. Step 1: Submit the AUC Graduate Admission Application Review the university’s graduate admission instructions and prepare the required documents. Then create an account or sign in through the AUC online application portal . Select the appropriate degree-seeking graduate-diploma program in public policy or public administration and complete every required section. Before submission, confirm that: The name and personal information on the application match the applicant’s official identity documents. Academic transcripts and proof of degree completion meet AUC’s official-document rules. Any document not issued in English has the required official translation. The statement of purpose is tailored to the selected program. Recommenders have enough time to submit their letters. English-proficiency results will remain valid through the first day of registered classes, as required by AUC. Step 2: Submit the Online Fellowship Application After addressing the graduate admission process, complete the separate fellowship application through the link provided on the official SFID listing . AUC’s fellowship button currently directs users to its Banner portal. Applicants should save confirmation pages or emails for both submissions. If the portals request different information, complete each form independently rather than assuming information transfers automatically between systems. How to Prepare a Strong Application The official page does not publish a detailed scoring rubric, so no applicant can guarantee selection. Nevertheless, candidates can present a clearer and more credible application by focusing on the qualities directly relevant to the fellowship’s stated design. 1. Demonstrate academic excellence with evidence The fellowship specifically targets applicants with excellent academic records. Use the CV, transcripts, statement of purpose, and recommendations to show consistent achievement, analytical ability, research experience, strong writing, or other evidence of readiness for graduate study. 2. Explain why the chosen diploma fits the applicant’s goals A generic statement is less useful than a focused explanation of why public policy or public administration is the appropriate field. Applicants should connect previous education, professional experience, volunteer work, research interests, or public-service ambitions to the diploma they select. 3. Show a credible interest in inclusive development Candidates can explain the social or policy challenges they hope to understand and address. The strongest discussion will be specific, grounded in experience, and connected to realistic academic and professional goals rather than relying on broad claims. 4. Address readiness for the Public Policy HUB commitment Because fellows must complete at least 12 working hours per week with the HUB, applicants should be ready to describe relevant strengths such as policy research, writing, data analysis, stakeholder engagement, communication, teamwork, or project coordination. They should also consider how they will balance this commitment with full-time study. 5. Choose recommenders strategically The general graduate checklist requires at least two recommendations. Suitable referees should know the applicant’s academic or professional work well enough to give concrete examples of performance, judgment, reliability, and potential for advanced study. 6. Start before the application window closes Official transcripts, English-language testing, translations, and recommendation letters can take time. Applicants should prepare these materials in advance and avoid treating the final day as the target submission date. Important Clarifications Before Applying Does the award fund a complete master’s degree? The fellowship provides full coverage for the credit hours needed for the eligible graduate diploma, up to nine credits per semester for two semesters. Diploma credits may count toward an MPP or MPA, but AUC does not state that this award covers the remaining requirements of either master’s degree. Is the fellowship open to applicants living outside Egypt? The official eligibility statement includes Egyptian nationals and refugees residing in Egypt from Yemen, Palestine, Syria, and Sudan. Refugee applicants should therefore not assume eligibility if they live outside Egypt. Can a refugee of any nationality apply? Not according to the published criteria. AUC expressly names Yemeni, Palestinian, Syrian, and Sudanese applicants among refugees residing in Egypt. Is a monthly stipend included? AUC’s published award list does not mention a stipend or living allowance. The listed support consists of eligible tuition, student services and activities fees, and medical service and health insurance fees. Is the award automatically renewed for the second semester? No. The two-semester duration is subject to review after the first semester for satisfactory academic performance, and fellows must maintain at least a 3.2 GPA. Is admission to AUC the same as receiving the fellowship? No. Candidates must complete the graduate admission application and the separate fellowship application. Admission eligibility is a requirement, while fellowship selection is a distinct funding decision. Where can applicants ask questions? AUC directs fellowship inquiries to gradserv@aucegypt.edu . Questions about unusual residency documentation, refugee status evidence, program-specific admission requirements, or unlisted expenses should be sent to AUC before the deadline. Final Application Checklist Before submitting, candidates should confirm that they have: Verified that they fall within one of the published nationality or refugee-status groups. Selected the Graduate Diploma in Public Policy or Graduate Diploma in Public Administration. Reviewed AUC’s general and program-specific graduate admission requirements. Prepared an official bachelor’s transcript and proof of degree completion. Arranged an official English translation for any credential not issued in English. Prepared a focused statement of purpose of about 500 words for each selected program. Updated their CV. Requested at least two recommendation letters. Confirmed the applicable English-proficiency requirements and test validity. Completed the graduate admission application. Completed the separate fellowship application. Submitted both processes before their respective deadlines. Planned for a full-time course load and at least 12 Public Policy HUB working hours each week. Understood the minimum 3.2 GPA continuation requirement. Budgeted for expenses not identified in the official award coverage. Conclusion The Swiss Fellowship for Inclusive Development at the American University in Cairo offers a focused route into graduate-level public policy or public administration study for academically excellent, eligible applicants. Its combination of tuition support, university fee coverage, health-related fee coverage, and practical work with the Public Policy HUB can help recipients develop both academic knowledge and applied policy experience. Applicants should approach the opportunity with a precise understanding of its scope. The award supports up to nine credits per semester for two semesters, requires full-time diploma enrollment, demands at least 12 hours of HUB work each week, and depends on maintaining a minimum 3.2 GPA. It is restricted to Egyptian nationals and specified refugee groups residing in Egypt, and it requires both an AUC graduate admission application and a separate fellowship application. For the Spring 2027 cycle, the fellowship application deadline is November 2, 2026. Prospective candidates should begin collecting academic records, recommendations, English-language evidence, and identity or residency documents well before the portal opens. All applicants should verify the current instructions and dates on AUC’s official website before submitting. For more global opportunities, click HERE . title: WMO Internship 2026 in Geneva: Paid Six-Month UN Opportunity in Partnerships, Climate and Resource Mobilization
summary: The World Meteorological Organization is accepting applications for a paid six-month internship in Geneva, Switzerland, within its Division of Development Partnerships and Programme Delivery. The placement offers an exceptional entry point into the United Nations system for a Master’s-level candidate interested in international partnerships, philanthropy, private-sector engagement, sustainable finance, climate action, resource mobilization, due diligence, strategic communications and high-level event coordination. The selected intern will join the Private Sector and Philanthropic Engagement Unit and work under the supervision of its Head. Rather than being limited to routine administrative support, the assignment covers partner research, meeting preparation, reputational-risk reviews, contributor engagement, briefing materials, knowledge management and support for major international platforms and events. Applications must be submitted through the official WMO recruitment portal by 22 September 2026 . The vacancy record is scheduled to close at 11:59 p.m. Geneva time . Candidates should apply early to avoid technical problems near the deadline. Full details are available on the official WMO vacancy page . WMO Internship 2026: Key Information Detail Information Host organization World Meteorological Organization Position Internship (INTERNSHIP-2026-DPPD 1) Job identification number 36754 Division Division of Development Partnerships and Programme Delivery Unit Private Sector and Philanthropic Engagement Unit Location Geneva, Switzerland Duration Six months Published Geneva stipend CHF 1,500 per month Experience No prior experience required Education Master’s level in a relevant field Required language Fluency in English Additional language French is advantageous Posting date 8 September 2026 Application deadline 22 September 2026 Application method WMO online e-recruitment system only The vacancy does not specify a starting date, number of openings, daily working schedule, relocation allowance or travel reimbursement. Applicants should not assume that costs not expressly covered by WMO’s published internship conditions will be paid. About the World Meteorological Organization The World Meteorological Organization is a specialized agency of the United Nations and the UN system’s authoritative voice on weather, climate and water. WMO supports international cooperation in meteorology, climatology, operational hydrology and related geophysical sciences. It provides a framework through which its 193 Member States and Territories exchange Earth-system information and strengthen services that protect lives, livelihoods, economies and the environment. Its Secretariat is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland. Learn more about WMO’s mandate . This institutional environment makes the internship particularly relevant for candidates seeking to understand how a UN specialized agency develops partnerships beyond governments. The intern will gain exposure to WMO’s engagement with companies, foundations, investors, philanthropies, academic organizations and other non-state stakeholders. About the Private Sector and Philanthropic Engagement Unit The Private Sector and Philanthropic Engagement Unit operates within WMO’s Division of Development Partnerships and Programme Delivery. The Unit coordinates WMO’s institutional engagement with private and non-state actors, including: Private-sector companies; Philanthropic foundations and philanthropists; Commercial entities and technology companies; Business and industry associations; Investors and prospective contributors; High-net-worth individuals; and Other organizations capable of contributing finance, expertise, technology or in-kind resources. The Unit’s responsibility extends beyond identifying donors. It cultivates high-impact partnerships and supports WMO technical departments and Members in pursuing appropriate, mutually beneficial cooperation with external organizations. That work requires accurate research, effective relationship management, sound documentation, reputational safeguards and an understanding of WMO’s public-interest mandate. WMO describes public-private engagement as cooperation among public institutions, businesses, academia and civil society in producing and delivering weather, climate, hydrological, marine and environmental information and services. Its approach emphasizes public value, integrity, mutual benefit, transparency, sovereignty and sustainability. Read about WMO’s public-private engagement framework . The WMO Commons The WMO Commons is WMO’s pooled financing mechanism. According to the vacancy announcement, it aims to mobilize USD 100 million over five years . The intern will help the Unit identify potential contributors and strategic partners, conduct background research and maintain materials used for contributor and investor engagement. This work will provide practical experience in international resource mobilization, including: Identifying potential contributors; Understanding organizational funding priorities; Assessing strategic alignment; Preparing cases for support; Developing partner profiles; Updating pitch materials; and Recording and following up on engagement. The Open Consultative Platform The Open Consultative Platform is WMO’s principal mechanism for structured dialogue with private-sector and academic stakeholders. It supports discussion about partnerships, innovation and the future of the global weather, climate and water enterprise. The intern will assist with the preparation and follow-up of platform sessions and other high-level engagements. Assignments may include preparing concept notes, researching participants, developing agendas, compiling briefing packages, coordinating participation, recording meeting outcomes and monitoring follow-up actions. Why WMO Is Recruiting for This Placement The Private Sector and Philanthropic Engagement Unit is managing a growing portfolio connected with the WMO Commons, the Open Consultative Platform and wider partnership-development work. At the same time, the Unit is preparing for several prominent international engagements, including: TECO Amsterdam in October 2026; The fourth session of WMO’s Services Commission, known as SERCOM-4; COP31 in Antalya in November 2026; and The World Economic Forum in January 2027. The vacancy explains that the volume and complexity of these workstreams exceed the Unit’s current staffing capacity. The selected intern will provide operational support in research, meeting coordination, documentation, due diligence and communications. Candidates should therefore expect a fast-moving environment involving several simultaneous assignments and deadlines. Detailed Duties and Responsibilities 1. Partnership engagement and meeting support The intern will help coordinate bilateral meetings involving companies, philanthropic foundations, investors and other non-state actors. Responsibilities will include: Preparing meeting agendas; Researching organizations and participants; Developing background notes and participant profiles; Taking accurate meeting notes; Converting discussions into structured summaries; Recording decisions and agreed actions; Following up on outstanding actions; Updating the Dialogue Tracker; Maintaining contact lists; and Keeping partner-engagement records current. This area of work requires discretion, organization and the ability to distinguish significant decisions and action points from general discussion. 2. Partnership research and resource mobilization The intern will research and map prospective private-sector and philanthropic partners, contributors and funding opportunities. This will involve: Identifying organizations whose priorities may align with WMO’s work; Preparing institutional and partner profiles; Monitoring developments in philanthropy and sustainable finance; Researching private-sector engagement trends; Comparing prospective contributors and opportunities; Identifying potential areas of cooperation; and Supporting the prioritization of partnership and resource-mobilization opportunities. Candidates who can transform extensive research into short, decision-useful notes will be particularly well suited to this responsibility. 3. Due diligence and reputational-risk support Before engaging an external organization, WMO must consider integrity, compliance and reputational risks. The intern will assist by: Conducting background research on companies, foundations and other prospective partners; Reviewing relevant public information and databases; Supporting the preparation of due-diligence reviews; Assisting with reputational-risk assessments; Documenting the information used in each review; and Maintaining due-diligence records and trackers according to WMO procedures. This responsibility is especially relevant for applicants interested in governance, compliance, corporate responsibility, legal research, ESG, ethical partnership management or reputational-risk analysis. 4. Support for the WMO Commons The intern will contribute to the operationalization and promotion of the WMO Commons. Expected assignments include: Mapping prospective contributors and strategic partners; Researching potential sources of financial and in-kind support; Updating pitch materials; Preparing frequently asked questions; Developing presentations and communication products; and Compiling background information for investor and contributor discussions. The intern will learn how an international organization formulates a financing proposition and communicates it to different external audiences. 5. High-level event support The intern will support Open Consultative Platform sessions and other major private-sector and philanthropic engagements. Tasks may include: Drafting or updating concept notes; Supporting agenda development; Researching participants; Preparing briefing documents; Maintaining logistical documentation; Coordinating with participants; Producing meeting reports; and Tracking post-event actions. The placement is therefore relevant to candidates interested in multistakeholder dialogue, international conferences, diplomacy, stakeholder coordination or strategic event management. 6. Strategic platforms and sector engagement The intern will support WMO’s involvement in private-sector platforms, professional networks and global forums. These may cover: Sustainable finance; Climate risk; Technology and innovation; Weather and climate services; Water services; and International development priorities. The intern will monitor upcoming opportunities and prepare concise background papers or briefing materials as required. 7. Briefings, communications and knowledge management The intern will help prepare written materials for senior-level engagements, including: Official correspondence; Briefing notes; Talking points; Presentations; and Internal reports. The intern will also maintain organized records of the Unit’s partnerships and activities and support information exchange with other WMO units and technical departments. Additional related responsibilities may be assigned by the supervisor. Educational Requirements The vacancy calls for Master’s-level education in one of the following areas: International relations; International development; Climate studies; Business; Economics; Law or legal studies; or Another related discipline. WMO’s broader internship programme is intended for students and recent graduates. For this opening, candidates should be pursuing or have recently completed Master’s-level studies in a relevant field. Applicants must describe their current degree status accurately. Incomplete studies should not be presented as a completed qualification. Experience Requirements No prior professional experience is required. This allows candidates to use evidence from academic study, research assignments, dissertations, volunteering, student organizations or extracurricular activities. Academic exposure to the following subjects would be advantageous: International organizations; Private-sector engagement; Partnership development; Resource mobilization; Philanthropy; Sustainable finance; or Sustainability. Candidates should not avoid applying merely because they have never worked for the United Nations. The announcement expressly states that previous professional experience is not required. Required Skills Applicants should demonstrate: Strong research ability; Strong professional writing skills; Ability to work in a multicultural environment; Close attention to detail; and Ability to organize and manage multiple assignments simultaneously. The duties also indicate the practical value of analytical writing, reliable recordkeeping, stakeholder awareness, professional communication, sound judgment and disciplined follow-up. Language Requirements Fluency in English is mandatory. The assignment involves research, correspondence, meeting records, briefing notes, talking points, presentations and internal reports. Candidates should therefore be able to communicate clearly and accurately in professional English. Knowledge of French is advantageous but is not identified as a mandatory requirement. WMO’s general internship guidance also states that knowledge of another UN language—Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian or Spanish—is desirable, although this particular vacancy specifically highlights French. Review the official WMO internship conditions . Learning and Professional Development The official vacancy identifies hands-on learning in public-private engagement at the international level. The selected intern can expect exposure to: Partnership development within a UN specialized agency; Private-sector and philanthropic engagement; Contributor research and resource mobilization; Due-diligence and reputational-risk processes; High-level meeting and event coordination; Strategic briefings and institutional communications; Stakeholder databases and knowledge-management systems; and Coordination among technical departments and external organizations. WMO’s general internship programme also aims to help participants: Understand WMO’s mandate; Learn applicable organizational rules and guidance; Develop an understanding of UN processes and policies; Complete mandatory training; Strengthen professional communication skills; Understand the challenges of working in a multicultural organization; and Build professional relationships and networks. Stipend, Leave and Insurance WMO’s published internship conditions state that interns recruited in Geneva receive CHF 1,500 per month . For a six-month placement, this would equal CHF 9,000 over the complete internship before considering any special institutional funding or insurance-related addition. Other published conditions include: If an intern is funded by a WMO Member State or university, the allowance follows the sending organization’s policy; Interns accrue 2.5 days of annual leave per month; A six-month appointment would therefore accrue 15 days of annual leave; Unused annual leave is not compensated when the internship ends; Health and accident insurance is mandatory for interns based in Switzerland; WMO recommends Swisscare for interns requiring sickness and accident insurance in Switzerland; The intern completes the enrollment, while WMO covers the expense by adding the insurance cost to the monthly stipend; Locally recruited interns who already have suitable insurance may opt out of Swisscare; Interns are covered by the WMO Benefits Insurance Plan and Malicious Act Insurance Policy; and If an intern is exceptionally required to travel for official work, accident and illness insurance applies to the travel. These are WMO’s general programme conditions. The selected candidate’s appointment letter will remain the controlling document for exact financial and insurance arrangements. Age, Diversity and Equal Opportunity The vacancy states that candidates must be at least 18 years old. It also mentions WMO’s statutory retirement age of 65 and requires an appointee to be able to complete the contract before reaching the mandatory age of separation. WMO is committed to diversity and a balanced workforce. Qualified women and men, including persons with disabilities, are encouraged to apply. No nationality, race, ethnicity or continental restriction is stated for this vacancy. WMO’s internship programme welcomes students and recent graduates from around the world. Its general internship guidance describes the programme’s potential audience as: Students approaching the end of their studies; Students who need an internship to complete their studies; Recent graduates; Early-career candidates with less than two years of relevant experience; Scholarship-supported interns; and Candidates sponsored by governments, NGOs or academic institutions. These general descriptions should be read together with the specific vacancy requirements, which state Master’s-level education, no prior experience requirement and a minimum age of 18. How to Apply Applications must be submitted through WMO’s online e-recruitment system. WMO does not accept applications by email or post. Candidates should follow these steps: Open the official vacancy page . Sign in to an existing candidate account or create a new profile. Complete all relevant profile sections, including education, language ability, academic projects and any work, volunteer or extracurricular experience. Demonstrate Master’s-level study in an eligible discipline. Provide evidence of research, writing, organization and multicultural teamwork. Review the profile for accuracy, completeness and consistency. Submit through the official portal only and avoid sending the application through multiple routes. Apply before 22 September 2026 , preferably well before the scheduled closing time. The public vacancy text does not prescribe a fixed package of supporting documents. Candidates should follow the document prompts presented inside the recruitment portal. WMO screens candidates using the information contained in their online profiles. Its official application guidance advises applicants to ensure that all information is complete and current before submission. Practical Tips for a Competitive Application These recommendations are based on the published responsibilities and are not additional eligibility conditions. Connect academic work to the assignment Candidates without extensive professional experience can use a thesis, capstone project, research paper or relevant coursework as evidence. Strong subject areas may include: Climate finance; Sustainable development; International organizations; Corporate responsibility; Philanthropy; Partnership models; Development economics; Compliance; or International law. Demonstrate decision-focused research Avoid merely stating that you possess research skills. Explain how you collected information, evaluated sources, identified risks or opportunities and converted findings into a clear output for a particular audience. Provide evidence of professional writing The role involves agendas, background notes, profiles, meeting summaries, briefing documents, talking points, presentations and reports. Highlight assignments or activities requiring accurate, concise and audience-appropriate writing. Show organization and follow-through The Unit needs support across several events and partnership workstreams. Provide an example of managing competing deadlines, maintaining records, coordinating participants or tracking actions through completion. Address due diligence and integrity Applicants with exposure to legal research, compliance, ESG, reputational-risk analysis, corporate governance or ethical screening should make that connection explicit. Academic experience can be relevant when it demonstrates careful evidence handling and balanced judgment. Highlight multicultural experience Evidence may come from international education, multicultural group projects, language learning, volunteer work, student associations or collaboration with people from different national and professional backgrounds. Describe language ability accurately English fluency is mandatory, while French is advantageous. Candidates should state their actual proficiency and support it with education, certification or practical experience where possible. Selection Process Only candidates in whom WMO has further interest will be contacted. Shortlisted applicants may be required to: Complete a written assessment; Attend an interview; or Participate in both stages. Selected candidates will undergo relevant checks and must comply with WMO’s professional standards and principles. WMO states that it does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination or abuse of authority. Important Clarification About the Probation Paragraph The vacancy contains a generic paragraph under the heading “Probation” referring to possible renewal after a one-year probationary period, potentially extendable to two years. That wording does not reconcile with: The vacancy’s specific six-month contract duration; or WMO’s general rule that internships last between three and twelve months. The most reasonable interpretation is that this is standard recruitment text inadvertently included in the vacancy template. It should not be treated as an entitlement to a one- or two-year internship. Applicants should rely on the stated six-month duration and seek clarification from the WMO Recruitment Helpdesk if this issue is material to their decision. Recruitment Scam Warning WMO does not charge an application, processing, interview, validation, appointment or training fee at any stage. The Organization also states that it will not ask applicants for bank-account information during recruitment. Candidates should apply only through the official recruitment portal and treat any payment request or unofficial offer claiming to guarantee selection as fraudulent. Application Deadline and Official Link Application deadline: 22 September 2026 Official application page: Apply through the WMO e-recruitment system Because the application period is short, interested candidates should create or update their WMO profile and submit well before the closing day. Conclusion The WMO Internship 2026 in Geneva is a valuable opportunity for a Master’s-level student or recent graduate seeking experience at the intersection of climate action, international development, private-sector engagement, philanthropy and institutional partnerships. The six-month placement combines substantive research with practical operational responsibilities. The selected intern will gain exposure to resource mobilization, reputational due diligence, high-level briefings, international events and collaboration across a United Nations specialized agency. No previous professional experience is required, but candidates must demonstrate research ability, strong writing, attention to detail, multicultural teamwork and the capacity to manage several assignments simultaneously. With a published Geneva stipend of CHF 1,500 per month and an application deadline of 22 September 2026, eligible applicants should review the official notice carefully and apply through WMO’s e-recruitment system without delay. title: 2027 Chase Leadership Development Program – Summer Analyst Opportunity in the USA
summary: The 2027 Chase Leadership Development Program (CLDP) Summer Analyst Opportunity is now open for students interested in gaining hands-on experience in financial services, business strategy, product development, project management, analytics, and emerging technology. Offered by JPMorgan Chase Co. through its Consumer Community Banking division, the program provides selected students with a 9-week summer analyst experience designed to introduce them to the Chase Leadership Development Program and prepare high-performing candidates for potential full-time opportunities after graduation. The 2027 Summer Analyst Program is available in Columbus, Ohio; Wilmington, Delaware; and Plano, Texas , giving eligible students an opportunity to gain practical corporate experience while working on projects that have a real-world impact on customers and the business. The application deadline is December 1, 2026, at 8:00 AM . However, applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, and the program may close earlier once available positions are filled. Students who meet the eligibility requirements are therefore strongly encouraged to apply as early as possible. What Is the Chase Leadership Development Program Summer Analyst Opportunity? The Chase Leadership Development Program Summer Analyst Opportunity is a summer internship experience within JPMorgan Chase s Consumer Community Banking business. The program is structured as a 9-week introduction to the full-time Chase Leadership Development Program . During the summer, analysts receive exposure to Chase s businesses and work on projects intended to provide measurable value to the organization and its customers. Rather than being limited to one narrow area of banking, the program provides exposure to a broad range of functions and business areas. These include: Auto Business Banking Card Services Connected Commerce Consumer Banking Digital Product Experience Finance Home Lending J.P. Morgan Wealth Management Marketing Controls Operations Risk Management Strategy and Strategic Initiatives Summer Analysts are placed into roles focused on one of three primary disciplines: Product Project/Program Management Strategy Strategic Initiatives This structure allows participants to develop a broader understanding of how a major financial institution develops products, manages complex projects, makes strategic decisions, evaluates risk, and serves customers. What Does a Chase Summer Analyst Do? The Summer Analyst role is designed to provide meaningful exposure to real business challenges rather than simply observational work. Participants may contribute to projects involving data, product development, strategy, marketing, operations, risk, technology, and cross-functional collaboration. Key responsibilities include: 1. Data Analytics and Business Decision-Making Summer Analysts may use data analytics to evaluate operational effectiveness and help support business decisions. This can involve: Measuring operational performance Analyzing business data Supporting risk-versus-reward decisions Assessing profitability Forecasting financial outcomes Identifying opportunities for improvement This component makes analytical ability particularly important for candidates interested in the program. 2. Product Development Participants may contribute to the development of financial products and services throughout their lifecycle. This can include: Testing new features Iterating products based on findings Measuring performance Evaluating customer response Supporting product marketing Helping develop new and emerging financial solutions Students interested in product management, technology, marketing, business development, or customer experience may find this particularly relevant. 3. Project and Program Management Analysts may also support project management efforts associated with high-visibility Chase brands and initiatives. This can include work related to: Marketing initiatives Media initiatives Business projects Cross-functional coordination Project planning Implementation Performance measurement The role therefore requires candidates who can organize information, manage priorities, collaborate with different teams, and help move projects forward. 4. Business Strategy and Regulatory Controls Summer Analysts may evaluate and quantify business strategies while taking regulatory controls into consideration. This provides exposure to the relationship between: Business strategy Financial performance Risk Regulation Operational controls Customer outcomes Students interested in strategy, finance, risk management, consulting, or financial services can gain valuable experience from this aspect of the program. 5. Cross-Functional Problem Solving The program emphasizes collaboration across different business functions. Depending on the assignment, analysts may work with teams such as: Engineering Brand Legal Compliance Finance UX Design Product Operations Strategy This provides participants with an opportunity to understand how large organizations bring together people with different technical and professional backgrounds to solve complex business problems. 6. AI-Enabled Solutions The 2027 program also highlights the use of artificial intelligence in business operations. Participants may have opportunities to: Design AI-enabled solutions Build and deploy solutions that automate workflows Improve decision-making Enhance customer and stakeholder experiences Evaluate AI models Monitor AI-enabled systems Apply responsible AI controls This makes the opportunity particularly relevant for students interested in the intersection of business, finance, analytics, technology, and artificial intelligence . Training and Professional Development One of the major features of the Chase Leadership Development Program Summer Analyst experience is its emphasis on professional development. Participants have access to structured training designed to strengthen both business knowledge and professional skills. The program provides a support network that includes: A dedicated program manager Professional mentors Senior leaders Managers Peer mentors Participants can also receive frequent feedback and coaching throughout the internship. This environment is intended to help students understand their strengths, improve their professional capabilities, develop their personal brand, and build meaningful professional relationships. Potential Pathway to a Full-Time Career The Summer Analyst Program can serve as an entry point into the broader Chase Leadership Development Program . Successful completion of the summer program may result in an offer of employment into the CLDP full-time program , which is described as a two-year rotational program . This is an important feature for students who are looking beyond a short-term internship and are interested in developing a longer-term career at JPMorgan Chase. However, completion of the summer program does not mean that every participant is automatically guaranteed a full-time position. The opportunity states that successful completion may result in an offer. Required Skills and Qualifications Candidates should demonstrate a combination of analytical ability, communication skills, professionalism, curiosity, and problem-solving ability. The required capabilities include: Analytical Skills Applicants should have exceptional analytical skills and demonstrate strong technical learning ability. Candidates should be comfortable learning new concepts and using information to understand and solve business problems. Intellectual Curiosity The program looks for students who demonstrate: Curiosity Willingness to learn Interest in understanding how businesses work Motivation to explore new ideas Microsoft Office Skills Applicants should be proficient in: Microsoft Excel Microsoft Word Microsoft PowerPoint These tools are important for analysis, documentation, presentations, and communicating business recommendations. Communication Skills Strong interpersonal and communication skills are required. Candidates should be able to communicate effectively with colleagues, managers, and other stakeholders. Teamwork and Collaboration The program operates in a highly collaborative environment, so candidates should be comfortable working as part of a team. title: Rio Changemakers Call for Funds: Apply to Join the First Global Climate and Nature Investment Cohort
summary: Rio Changemakers is inviting impact funds focused on climate and nature to apply to become part of the first cohort featured on a new global marketplace designed to connect trusted investment opportunities with investors and locally led projects. The initiative aims to strengthen connections between climate and nature-focused capital and credible organizations working on solutions in emerging markets and developing economies. Funds selected for the first cohort will have the opportunity to help shape the platform while increasing their visibility among potential investors and accessing a growing pipeline of locally led projects seeking financing. Priority consideration deadline: 26 September 2026 About Rio Changemakers Rio Changemakers is an AI-enabled, science-guided marketplace being developed by the Government of Luxembourg and the Global Landscapes Forum (GLF) . The platform is being designed to address an important challenge in climate and nature finance: connecting credible, locally led initiatives with appropriate financing partners. The marketplace aims to make it easier for: Investors to discover trusted climate and nature investment opportunities. Locally led projects to connect with potential financing partners. Impact funds to increase their visibility among investors. Capital to reach organizations and communities already leading climate and nature action. The initiative places particular emphasis on locally led action across emerging markets and developing economies . What Is the Rio Changemakers Call for Funds? Rio Changemakers is looking for impact funds that invest in climate and nature solutions and are committed to supporting locally led action. Selected funds will become part of the platform s first cohort . This means selected organizations will have an early opportunity to interact with and test the marketplace while contributing feedback that can help improve the platform before it grows further. The call is therefore not simply an opportunity for funds to gain visibility. It is also an opportunity to participate in the development of a global financing platform intended to improve access to capital for locally led climate and nature initiatives. Who Should Apply? The call is specifically aimed at impact funds rather than individual applicants, NGOs applying for grants, students, researchers or individual entrepreneurs. Funds should have an investment strategy focused on climate and/or nature solutions and demonstrate a commitment to supporting locally led action. Rio Changemakers particularly welcomes funds that support: Indigenous Peoples Local communities Women-led organizations Youth-led organizations Other locally led initiatives Priority will also be given to funds investing in specific regions of the Global South and other emerging and developing markets. Priority Regions Rio Changemakers states that priority will be given to funds investing in: Africa Asia Latin America The Pacific The Caribbean Funds working across multiple regions may therefore be particularly relevant, especially where their investment strategies support locally led climate and nature solutions. What Types of Funds Are Encouraged to Apply? The initiative is looking for funds whose investment activities align with climate, nature and locally led development. Potentially relevant funds may include those investing in areas such as: Climate solutions Nature-based solutions Biodiversity Conservation Sustainable land management Sustainable agriculture Climate resilience Community-led environmental initiatives Locally led development Women s climate initiatives Youth-led climate initiatives Indigenous-led environmental initiatives Other climate and nature-related solutions The key consideration is whether the fund s investment strategy aligns with the objectives of Rio Changemakers. Why Join the First Rio Changemakers Cohort? Being selected for the first cohort can provide several potential benefits to participating funds. 1. Early Access to the Marketplace Selected funds will be among the first organizations to use the Rio Changemakers platform. They will have an opportunity to create their fund profile and experience the platform before it expands further. 2. Increased Visibility As Rio Changemakers develops its global marketplace, participating funds will have an opportunity to increase their visibility among investors looking for credible climate and nature investment opportunities. A presence on the platform could help funds communicate their: Investment strategy Areas of focus Geographic priorities Climate and nature objectives Approach to locally led investment 3. Access to a Growing Project Pipeline The platform is intended to connect funds and investors with a growing pipeline of credible, locally led climate and nature projects seeking financing . For participating funds, this could create opportunities to discover potential investment opportunities that align with their strategies. 4. Help Shape the Platform First-cohort participants will not simply use the platform. They will also be asked to test key features and provide feedback . Their feedback can help inform the development of a marketplace that better serves both: Investors and impact funds; and Locally led organizations seeking financing. 5. Contribute to a Global Public Good Rio Changemakers describes the marketplace as a public good intended to help make it easier for capital to reach local people and organizations already leading climate and nature action. By participating, funds can therefore contribute to a broader effort to improve the connection between capital and locally led climate and nature solutions. How the Application Process Works Interested impact funds are asked to complete an online questionnaire. The questionnaire is designed to help Rio Changemakers understand the applicant s: Fund structure Investment strategy Areas of focus Geographic priorities Approach to climate and nature investment Commitment to locally led action Readiness to participate in the first cohort Applicants should provide accurate and complete information. Where a question provides several options, applicants should select all applicable options unless the question specifically states otherwise . How Long Does the Application Take? The organizers estimate that the questionnaire will take approximately 15–20 minutes to complete. Applicants are encouraged to prepare the relevant information about their fund and investment strategy before beginning the questionnaire. Application Review Process Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis . This means applicants do not necessarily need to wait until the final deadline to apply. However, Rio Changemakers encourages interested funds to submit their applications by: 26 September 2026 for priority consideration . Funds interested in joining the first cohort should therefore consider submitting their applications as early as possible. What Happens If Your Fund Is Selected? Selected funds will become part of the first Rio Changemakers cohort. As a participating organization, your fund will have the opportunity to: Create a profile on the marketplace. Test important platform features. Provide feedback on the platform. Help identify ways the marketplace can better serve investors and locally led organizations. Increase visibility among potential investors. Potentially connect with a growing pipeline of locally led climate and nature projects seeking financing. This makes the opportunity particularly relevant to funds that want to play an active role in shaping the future of climate and nature finance. Why Locally Led Climate and Nature Finance Matters One of the central ideas behind Rio Changemakers is the need to improve connections between financing and the people and organizations closest to climate and nature challenges. Locally led organizations often have deep knowledge of their communities and ecosystems and may be directly involved in developing and implementing solutions. The marketplace is intended to make it easier for investors to discover credible opportunities while helping locally led initiatives connect with financing partners. This approach places local actors at the center of climate and nature action rather than treating them simply as beneficiaries of externally designed projects. Geographic Focus Although the initiative has a global ambition, priority will be given to funds investing in Africa, Asia, Latin America, the Pacific and the Caribbean . Funds with significant investment activity in these regions should therefore pay particular attention to this opportunity. The geographic focus also makes the call especially relevant to impact funds supporting climate and nature solutions in developing and emerging economies. Click HERE to read more and apply. Application Deadline Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis . For priority consideration , impact funds are encouraged to apply by: 26 September 2026 The questionnaire takes approximately 15–20 minutes to complete. Conclusion The Rio Changemakers Call for Funds offers climate and nature-focused impact funds an opportunity to become part of the first cohort of an emerging global marketplace connecting investors with credible, locally led projects. The initiative is particularly relevant to funds investing in Africa, Asia, Latin America, the Pacific and the Caribbean , as well as funds supporting Indigenous Peoples, local communities, women-led organizations, youth-led organizations and other locally led initiatives. Selected funds will gain an opportunity to create a profile, test the platform, provide feedback, increase their visibility among investors and potentially connect with a growing pipeline of climate and nature projects seeking financing. With applications reviewed on a rolling basis, interested impact funds are encouraged to submit their applications by 26 September 2026 for priority consideration . title: Pitch Perfect Africa 2026: CAD $5,000 Innovation Fellowship Opportunity for African Health Entrepreneurs
summary: Applications are now open for Pitch Perfect Africa 2026 , a competitive pitching opportunity designed to support early-stage entrepreneurs developing innovative solutions to health-related challenges across Africa. Now in its second year, Pitch Perfect Africa provides selected ventures with an opportunity to present their innovations to experienced judges, strengthen their investment readiness, gain valuable pitching experience, and compete for financial support to further develop their work. The 2026 edition will select six H2i Level 2 ventures to participate in the virtual pitch competition. From these finalists, three ventures will each receive a CAD $5,000 Innovation Fellowship , providing financial support for the continued development of their ventures. The program is designed and implemented by the Health Innovation Hub (H2i) under the Africa Health Collaborative , in partnership with the Mastercard Foundation . What Is Pitch Perfect Africa 2026? Pitch Perfect Africa is a pitch competition created specifically to provide early-stage ventures within the H2i community with access to funding, pitching opportunities, mentorship-oriented learning, and investment-readiness development . The initiative recognizes that early-stage health ventures often need more than financial resources to grow. Entrepreneurs also need to be able to clearly communicate their problem, solution, target market, competitive advantage, milestones, and team to potential investors, customers, partners, and other stakeholders. Through the competition, participating ventures get the opportunity to practice these skills in a competitive environment while presenting their innovations to a panel of expert judges. The Africa edition of Pitch Perfect was introduced to the H2i African venture community in 2025 and is continuing in 2026. What Does Pitch Perfect Africa 2026 Offer? The competition provides selected ventures with several valuable opportunities for development. 1. Opportunity to Pitch to Expert Judges Six eligible H2i Level 2 ventures will be selected to pitch their innovations to a panel of expert judges. This provides entrepreneurs with an opportunity to communicate their venture to an experienced audience and receive exposure through a formal pitch competition. 2. CAD $5,000 Innovation Fellowship Three of the six ventures selected to pitch will be awarded an Innovation Fellowship worth CAD $5,000 each . The funding is intended to support the continued development of the winning ventures and their work. Applicants should note that fellowship payments may take approximately three to four months after the competition to be processed. 3. Investment-Readiness Development Pitch Perfect Africa is not simply about winning funding. The competition is also intended to help early-stage ventures become better prepared to engage with potential investors and other stakeholders. Through the pitch preparation process, entrepreneurs can strengthen their ability to explain: The problem their venture is addressing Their proposed solution Their value proposition Their target market Their competitors Their business or venture milestones Their team Their broader opportunity for growth These are important areas for entrepreneurs seeking customers, partnerships, investment, or additional funding. 4. Pitching Experience For early-stage entrepreneurs, the ability to deliver a clear and convincing pitch can be just as important as having a strong idea. Pitch Perfect Africa gives participating ventures a structured environment in which they can practice presenting their work, communicating their value, and responding to an expert audience. Who Can Apply for Pitch Perfect Africa 2026? The eligibility requirements for Pitch Perfect Africa 2026 are specific. Applicants must meet the following requirements: Current H2i Level 2 Venture Applicants must be a current H2i Level 2 HENT venture that was onboarded by its lead mentor by August 31, 2026 . The organizers state that this requirement has no exceptions . H2i Level 2 ventures are described as ventures in the Discovery stage of H2i s four-level venture development model. Therefore, this is not an open competition for every health entrepreneur in Africa. Applicants must already meet the specified H2i Level 2 venture requirement. Previous Winners Are Not Eligible Ventures that have previously won Pitch Perfect Africa cannot apply again. However, past finalists who did not win are welcome to reapply . Ventures Outside the H2i Community Entrepreneurs and ventures that are not currently part of the H2i community are encouraged to join the H2i community as a client company. Joining the H2i community can provide access to: Mentorship Programs Venture development support Future opportunities However, simply being interested in the program does not mean a venture automatically qualifies for the 2026 competition. The specific H2i Level 2 eligibility requirement must be met. Who Is This Opportunity Designed For? Pitch Perfect Africa 2026 is designed for early-stage health entrepreneurs and health-focused ventures within the H2i African venture community , particularly ventures at the Level 2 Discovery stage. The opportunity is particularly relevant to entrepreneurs who: Are developing health-focused innovations Are currently recognized as eligible H2i Level 2 HENT ventures Want to strengthen their venture s pitch Want to improve investment readiness Are preparing to communicate their innovation to investors, customers, partners, experts, and judges Are interested in competing for financial support to continue developing their work APPLY HERE Geographic Eligibility The program is specifically connected to H2i s African venture community and is designed for African health innovation ventures within the H2i ecosystem. The information provided does not list a country-by-country eligibility list or restrict applications to particular African nationalities . Therefore, the source supports describing this as an Africa-focused opportunity for eligible H2i ventures , rather than claiming that every health entrepreneur from every African country can independently apply. The most important eligibility condition is the requirement to be a qualifying H2i Level 2 HENT venture onboarded by the lead mentor by August 31, 2026. The source also does not specify any restriction based on race or ethnicity. Important Dates for Pitch Perfect Africa 2026 Applicants should carefully take note of the competition timeline. H2i x University of Toronto Libraries Market Research Workshop Date and details: Coming soon A market research workshop is also planned in collaboration with the University of Toronto Libraries. Building a Winning Pitch Masterclass Friday, October 9, 2026 8:00–9:00 AM ET | 12:00–1:00 PM GMT The session will take place virtually through Zoom. Pitch Competition Monday, November 16, 2026 The main Pitch Perfect Africa 2026 competition will be held virtually. Visit HERE to learn more about the Pitch Perfect Africa 2026 How to Apply Eligible ventures should complete the Pitch Perfect Africa 2026 application form . Applicants are encouraged to prepare their answers before beginning the submission process. The organizers recommend drafting and saving responses in a separate document before submitting the final application. This can help applicants: Review their answers carefully. Make sure all required information is included. Improve the clarity of their responses. Avoid losing work while completing the application. Present their venture consistently throughout the application. For questions about the competition or application process, applicants can contact the organizers through the provided H2i email address: h2i.international@utoronto.ca . Preparing for the Pitch Pitch Perfect Africa 2026 also includes learning opportunities designed to help ventures prepare for the competition. One of the key preparation sessions is the Building a Winning Pitch Masterclass . Building a Winning Pitch Masterclass The masterclass is designed to help early-stage health entrepreneurs improve how they communicate their ventures. It will be led by Professor Paul Santerre and will focus on the 10 key elements of a winning pitch . The session will cover areas including: Defining the problem Explaining the solution Communicating the venture s value proposition Understanding the market Assessing competition Presenting milestones Explaining the team Strengthening the overall venture story The goal is to help entrepreneurs communicate more effectively with different audiences, including: Customers Experts Partners Judges Investors Masterclass Details Date: Friday, October 9, 2026 Time: 8:00–9:00 AM ET | 12:00–1:00 PM GMT Format: Zoom Registration: The masterclass registration is available through the provided Luma registration page. Entrepreneurs need to be able to communicate their ideas in a way that allows an audience to quickly understand: What problem exists Why the problem matters Who is affected What the venture is offering Why the proposed solution is different Who the customers or beneficiaries are What the market opportunity looks like What progress has already been made What the venture plans to achieve next Why the team is capable of delivering the solution For an early-stage venture, developing these communication skills can be valuable beyond this particular competition.
